PURPOSE, OBJECTIVE, AND BACKGROUND OF WORK TO BE PERFORMED: THE FOLLOWING TASK DESCRIPTIONS ARE IN SUPPORT OF THE SYSTEM LEVEL TOOLS&CONCEPT DESIGN SUB-PROJECT OF THE NASA FUNDAMENTAL AERONAUTICS HIGH SPEED PROJECT. THE OVERALL EFFORT IS FOCUSED ON IMPROVING THE DESIGN CYCLE TIME AND UNCERTAINTY IN LOW BOOM SUPERSONIC VEHICLE DESIGN. THE NEED FOR ROBUST MULTI-FIDELITY DESIGN AND ANALYSIS TOOLS FOR SONIC BOOM WILL ENABLE IMPROVED CYCLE TIME WITH MORE ACCURATE PREDICTIONS OF OVERALL SONIC BOOM LEVELS. IN ORDER TO REDUCE THE OVERALL SONIC BOOM LEVELS AND ALLOW PRACTICAL SUPERSONIC FLIGHT OVER LAND, IMPROVED ALGORITHMS WILL BE NEEDED FOR PERFORMING EFFICIENT DESIGN OPTIMIZATION AND RE-DESIGN. IN ADDITION, THOROUGH UNDERSTANDING OF THE UNDERLYING PHYSICAL PRINCIPLES OF ATMOSPHERIC PROPAGATION, BETTER TARGET GENERATION, CONSIDERATION OF OFF-TRACK EFFECTS AND OTHER INTEGRATION CHALLENGES NEED TO BE ADDRESSED. THE CURRENT SONIC BOOM PROPAGATION PROCESS USES ADVANCED PROPAGATION MECHANISMS TO BE ABLE TO ACCURATELY PREDICT BOTH THE UNDER-TRACK AND OFF-TRACK BOOM SIGNATURES. THIS, COUPLED WITH AUTOMATED OFF-BODY COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS (CFD) ANALYSIS, REPRESENTS THE STATE OF THE ART IN TERMS OF SONIC BOOM ANALYSIS. THE NEEDED WORK IS IN THE DESIGN PROCESS TO ACHIEVE FEASIBLE AIRCRAFT CONCEPTS THAT HAVE LOW SONIC BOOM LEVELS. AS SUCH, WORK IS NEEDED TO STEER BASELINE CONCEPTS TOWARDS OPTIMAL DESIGNS THAT REDUCE THE BOOM LOUDNESS WHILE IMPROVING OR NOT SIGNIFICANTLY DETERIORATING OTHER PERFORMANCE METRICS RELATED TO SUPERSONIC FLIGHT. IT FOCUSES ON A NEW STRUCTURAL CONCEPT THAT INTEGRATES SKIN, STRINGERS, AND FRAME ELEMENTS INTO A SINGLE LARGE PANEL IN WHICH ALL ELEMENTS ARE SIMULTANEOUSLY CURED (OR CO-CURED) IN ONE HIGH-TEMPERATURE CURE CYCLE. THE RESULTING STRUCTURE IS A NOVEL SOLUTION FOR ADDRESSING THE DEMANDING FUSELAGE LOADING REQUIREMENTS INHERENT IN A PRESSURIZED SHAPED VEHICLE LIKE THE HYBRID WING BODY (HWB) CONCEPT. THE PRSEUS CONCEPT BUILDS UPON, EXTENDS, AND TAILORS THESE STRUCTURAL TECHNOLOGIES IN ORDER TO MEET THE DEMANDING CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH VEHICLES WITH SHAPES AND LOAD PATHS DIFFERENT FROM TODAY S TRADITIONAL WING AND CIRCULAR FUSELAGE STRUCTURES. THE HIGH SPEED PROJECT ALSO HAS A TECHNICAL CHALLENGE OF ACHIEVING ACCEPTABLE AIRPORT COMMUNITY NOISE.
